'''Ravi Iyengar''' is a biochemist and [[systems biology|systems biologist]] and [[Pharmacology|pharmacologist]] and professor at the [[Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai]] in New York City. He directs the Mount Sinai Institute for Systems Biomedicine and lead the Systems Biology Center of New York, a [[Transdisciplinarity|transdisciplinary]] research center supported by the [[National Institute of General Medical Sciences]].<ref name="IcahnProfile">{{cite web |title=Srinivas (Ravi) Iyengar, PhD |url=https://profiles.icahn.mssm.edu/srinivas-ravi-iyengar |website=Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref><ref name="SBCNY">{{cite web |title=Systems Biology Center of New York |url=https://icahn.mssm.edu/research/systems-biology-center-ny |website=Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref>

Iyengar is known for integrating experimental biochemistry with computational modeling to study how cells process information through [[cell signaling|cell-signaling]] networks. His research has described emergent properties of signaling pathways and how network structure can produce complex behavior in [[mammal]]ian cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bhalla |first1=U. S. |last2=Iyengar |first2=R. |title=Emergent properties of networks of biological signaling pathways |journal=Science |year=1999 |volume=283 |issue=5400 |pages=381–387 |doi=10.1126/science.283.5400.381 |pmid=9888852 |bibcode=1999Sci...283..381B |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jordan |first1=J. D. |last2=Landau |first2=E. M. |last3=Iyengar |first3=R. |title=Signaling networks: The origins of cellular multitasking |journal=Cell |year=2000 |volume=103 |issue=2 |pages=193–200 |doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(00)00112-4|pmc=3619409 }}</ref> He holds four patents and edited six books.

==Education and career==

=== Education ===
Iyengar completed undergraduate and master's degrees at the [[University of Mumbai]] and earned graduate degrees at the [[University of Houston]], followed by postdoctoral training at [[Baylor College of Medicine]].<ref name="IcahnProfile" />

=== Professional ===
At Mount Sinai, he served as chair of the Department of Pharmacology (later Pharmacology and Biological Chemistry) and as of 2026 holds the Dorothy H. and Lewis Rosenstiel Professorship.<ref name="PharmHighlights">{{cite web |title=Pharmacology & Systems – Scientific Highlights |url=https://icahn.mssm.edu/about/departments/pharmacological-sciences/scientific-highlights |website=Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref> He also served as dean of research of the medical school in the early 2000s.<ref name="NIGMSBioBeat">{{cite web |title=Meet Ravi Iyengar |url=https://nigms.nih.gov/biobeat/2014/03/meet-ravi-iyengar |website=National Institute of General Medical Sciences |publisher=National Institutes of Health |date=March 5, 2014 |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref> He has also served as Director of the Experimental Therapeutics Institute (ETI) at Mount Sinai.<ref name="MSNewsroom2009TR01">{{cite web |date=September 24, 2009 |title=Mount Sinai Research Team Leads NIH-Funded Project Examining the Mechanism of Human Tissue Assembly |url=https://www.mountsinai.org/about/newsroom/2009/mount-sinai-research-team-leads-nihfunded-project-examining-the-mechanism-of-human-tissue-assembly |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=Mount Sinai - New York}}</ref> In 2009, he led a multi–principal investigator project funded through the NIH Transformative Research Projects (T-R01) program focused on assembling functional human kidney tissue in vitro using computational modeling and nanofabrication.<ref name="MSNewsroom2009TR01" /> A member of the Mount Sinai faculty since 1986.<ref name="Jacobi2018Iyengar">{{cite web |title=The Jacobi Medallion: Honoring Excellence |url=https://health.mountsinai.org/blog/the-jacobi-medallion-honoring-excellence/ |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=Mount Sinai Today}}</ref>

Iyengar is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref name="NASEMBio">{{cite book |title=Accelerating the Development of Biomarkers for Drug Safety: Workshop Summary |publisher=National Academies Press |year=2009 |chapter=Appendix B: Speaker Biographies |access-date=January 2, 2026 |chapter-url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/12587/chapter/9}}</ref>

=== Teaching and online education ===
Iyengar has published teaching resources on graduate education in cell signaling and quantitative modeling in ''Science'' and in ''Science Signaling'' (formerly ''Science STKE''), including course materials and approaches for using journal clubs and online asynchronous discussion as an assessment tool.<ref name="IyengarSTKE2005">{{cite journal |last1=Iyengar |first1=R. |last2=Diverse-Pierluissi |first2=M. |last3=Weinstein |first3=D. |last4=Devi |first4=L. A. |date=2005-02-01 |title=Teaching resources. Cell signaling systems: a course for graduate students |journal=Sci STKE |issue=269 |pages=tr3 |doi=10.1126/stke.2692005tr3 |pmid=15687508}}</ref><ref name="IyengarSciSignal2008Modeling">{{cite journal |last=Iyengar |first=R. |year=2008 |title=Teaching resource. Quantitative models of mammalian cell signaling pathways |journal=Science Signaling |volume=1 |issue=7 |pages=tr1 |doi=10.1126/stke.17tr1 |pmid=18290302}}</ref><ref name="JenkinsSciSignal2008Forums">{{cite journal |last1=Jenkins |first1=S. L. |year=2008 |title=Teaching resources. Using web-based discussion forums as a model of the peer-review process and a tool for assessment |journal=Science Signaling |volume=1 |issue=9 |pages=tr2 |doi=10.1126/stke.19tr2 |pmid=18323015}}</ref> He also co-authored a ''Science'' article describing an inquiry-learning format that integrated expert lectures, journal clubs, and web-based discussion forums to support critical reasoning and [[Peer review|peer-review]] skills in graduate training.<ref name="IyengarScience2008Inquiry">{{cite journal |last1=Iyengar |first1=R. |last2=Diverse-Pierluissi |first2=M. A. |last3=Jenkins |first3=S. L. |last4=Chan |first4=A. M. |last5=Devi |first5=L. A. |last6=Sobie |first6=E. A. |last7=Ting |first7=A. T. |last8=Weinstein |first8=D. C. |date=2008-02-29 |title=Inquiry learning. Integrating content detail and critical reasoning by peer review |journal=Science |volume=319 |issue=5867 |pages=1189–1190 |doi=10.1126/science.1149875 |pmc=3038128 |pmid=18309063}}</ref>

In 2012, Mount Sinai announced an agreement with Coursera to offer graduate and medical school coursework online beginning in 2013, and identified Iyengar as leading the initiative.<ref name="MSSMCoursera2012">{{cite web |date=September 19, 2012 |title=Mount Sinai School of Medicine Bringing Free Courses Online |url=https://www.mountsinai.org/about/newsroom/2012/mount-sinai-school-of-medicine-bringing-free-courses-online |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=Mount Sinai - New York}}</ref>

==Research==
Iyengar's laboratory combines experimental measurements with computational and mathematical modeling to study signaling network topology, regulatory motifs (e.g., feedback and feedforward loops), and spatial organization of signaling processes in cells and tissues.<ref name="IcahnProfile" /> Through the Systems Biology Center of New York, he has helped develop and disseminate systems approaches to [[Pathophysiology|pathophysiological]] processes, [[drug action]], and adverse event prediction, linking network methods to precision medicine applications.<ref name="SBCNY" />

His work has also been associated with the development of [[systems pharmacology]] approaches for understanding adverse events and drug effects at the network level.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Berger |first1=S. I. |last2=Iyengar |first2=R. |title=Network analyses in systems pharmacology |journal=Bioinformatics |year=2009 |volume=25 |issue=19 |pages=2466–2472 |doi=10.1093/bioinformatics/btp465 |pmid=19648136 |pmc=2752618 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Berger |first1=S. I. |last2=Iyengar |first2=R. |title=Role of systems pharmacology in understanding drug adverse events |journal=Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews: Systems Biology and Medicine |year=2011 |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=129–135 |doi=10.1002/wsbm.114 |pmid=20803507 |pmc=3057924 }}</ref>

Iyengar's research focuses on how cells process information through interconnected [[Cell signaling|cell-signaling]] networks, combining biochemical experiments with computational modeling. He and colleagues described how different [[adenylyl cyclase]] [[Protein isoform|isoforms]] have distinct functional properties and tissue distributions, allowing cells to tailor the integrative properties of [[Cyclic adenosine monophosphate|cAMP]] signaling by varying isoform expression.<ref name="Pieroni1993">{{cite journal |last1=Pieroni |first1=J. P. |last2=Jacobowitz |first2=O. |last3=Chen |first3=J. |last4=Iyengar |first4=R. |title=Signal recognition and integration by Gs-stimulated adenylyl cyclases |journal=Current Opinion in Neurobiology |date=1993 |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=345–351 |doi=10.1016/0959-4388(93)90127-K |pmid=8369627}}</ref> Iyengar discussed showed an expanded role for cAMP as a "gating" mechanism between signaling pathways.<ref name="Iyengar1996">{{cite journal |last=Iyengar |first=R. |date=1996-01-26 |title=Gating by cyclic AMP: expanded role for an old signaling pathway |journal=Science |volume=271 |issue=5248 |pages=461–463 |doi=10.1126/science.271.5248.461 |pmid=8560257 |bibcode=1996Sci...271..461L }}</ref> He later co-authored work reporting that cAMP-dependent regulation of [[protein phosphatase 1]] can gate [[CaMKII]] signaling during [[long-term potentiation]] in [[Hippocampus|hippocampal]] neurons.<ref name="Blitzer1998">{{cite journal |last1=Blitzer |first1=R. D. |last2=Connor |first2=J. H. |last3=Brown |first3=G. P. |last4=Wong |first4=T. |last5=Shenolikar |first5=S. |last6=Iyengar |first6=R. |date=1998-06-19 |title=Gating of CaMKII by cAMP-regulated protein phosphatase activity during LTP |journal=Science |volume=280 |issue=5371 |pages=1940–1943 |doi=10.1126/science.280.5371.1940 |pmid=9632393 |bibcode=1998Sci...280.1940B }}</ref>

Iyengar has also published modeling work on emergent behaviors in signaling networks, including feedback-driven [[bistability]] and threshold responses.<ref name="BhallaIyengar1999">{{cite journal |last1=Bhalla |first1=U. S. |last2=Iyengar |first2=R. |date=1999-01-15 |title=Emergent properties of networks of biological signaling pathways |journal=Science |volume=283 |issue=5400 |pages=381–387 |doi=10.1126/science.283.5400.381 |pmid=9888852 |bibcode=1999Sci...283..381B |doi-access=free }}</ref> He co-authored a graph-theoretic analysis of a mammalian signaling network model of hippocampal CA1 neurons that identified recurring regulatory motifs such as feedback and feedforward loops.<ref name="Maayan2005">{{cite journal |last1=Ma'ayan |first1=A. |last2=Jenkins |first2=S. L. |last3=Neves |first3=S. |last4=Hasseldine |first4=A. |last5=Grace |first5=E. |last6=Dubin-Thaler |first6=B. |last7=Eungdamrong |first7=N. J. |last8=Weng |first8=G. |last9=Ram |first9=P. T. |last10=Rice |first10=J. J. |last11=Kershenbaum |first11=A. |last12=Stolovitzky |first12=G. A. |last13=Blitzer |first13=R. D. |last14=Iyengar |first14=R. |date=2005-08-12 |title=Formation of regulatory patterns during signal propagation in a mammalian cellular network |journal=Science |volume=309 |issue=5737 |pages=1078–1083 |doi=10.1126/science.1108876 |pmc=3032439 |pmid=16099987 |bibcode=2005Sci...309.1078M }}</ref>

In the 2020s, Iyengar has been a co-author on Kidney Precision Medicine Project consortium studies developing single-cell and spatial reference atlases of human kidney tissue, including a reference tissue atlas and an integrated multimodal atlas of healthy and injured cell states and tissue "niches."<ref name="Hansen2022">{{cite journal |last1=Hansen |first1=J. |last2=Sealfon |first2=R. |last3=Menon |first3=R. |last4=Eadon |first4=M. T. |last5=Lake |first5=B. B. |last6=Steck |first6=B. |date=2022-06-10 |title=A reference tissue atlas for the human kidney |journal=Science Advances |volume=8 |issue=23 |article-number=eabn4965 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.abn4965 |pmc=9176741 |pmid=35675394 |bibcode=2022SciA....8N4965H }}</ref><ref name="Lake2023">{{cite journal |last1=Lake |first1=B. B. |last2=Menon |first2=R. |last3=Winfree |first3=S. |last4=Hu |first4=Q. |last5=Diep |first5=D. |last6=Kalhor |first6=K. |title=An atlas of healthy and injured cell states and niches in the human kidney |journal=Nature |date=2023 |volume=619 |issue=7970 |pages=585–594 |doi=10.1038/s41586-023-05769-3 |pmc=10356613 |pmid=37468583 |bibcode=2023Natur.619..585L }}</ref>

==Publications==

=== Editorial ===
Iyengar served as editor-in-chief of ''IET Systems Biology'' (2007–2009) and editor of the journal ''Systems Biology''.<ref name="NASEM2009Bio">{{cite web |title=Accelerating the Development of Biomarkers for Drug Safety: Workshop Summary – Appendix B: Speaker Biographies |url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/12587/chapter/9 |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=National Academies Press}}</ref> He is also editor of the journal ''Systems Biology''.<ref name="npjEditors">{{cite web |title=About the Editors |url=https://www.nature.com/npjsba/editors |website=npj Systems Biology and Applications |publisher=Springer Nature |access-date=January 2, 2026}}</ref>
